title: The named theorems people ask for — 19 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
The named theorems people ask for. 19 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/demand3.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 8 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 11 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 2 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 46 pairs; the theorems fall into 7 strands, the largest of 9. Most binding: repunit (9), chi (5).

2 · Imports. Built on: demand.lean, sequences.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 5 files: src/proof/demand3.lean, src/proof/demand.lean, src/proof/families.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean, src/proof/sequences.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 19 sealed receipts fold to ad3b6564-c548-8496-9743-0f38398dba8a. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (4, 6, 6, 0, 6, 7, 7). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: index.lean (5 observed, 1.79 expected, lift 2.79), address.lean (10 observed, 4.07 expected, lift 2.45), ledgerclaims.lean (3 observed, 1.3 expected, lift 2.3). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.56 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 44.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.86; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.55. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 78375f1a602d (2026-09-15), over 817 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Legendre’s three-square theorem — Adrien-Marie Legendre, 1797; Carmichael numbers — Robert Carmichael, 1910; amicable pairs — known to antiquity. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. wilsons_theorem_and_its_converse — ((List.range' 2 18).all (fun p => ¬ isPrime p || Sequences.fact (p - 1) % p == p - 1)) ∧ ((List.range' 5 15).all (fun n => isPrime n || Sequences.fact (n - 1) % n == 0)) record
  2. every_number_is_a_sum_of_four_squares — (List.range 60).all isSumOfFour ∧ isSumOfThree 7 = false ∧ isSumOfFour 7 = true record
  3. the_cantor_pairing_is_injective_and_covers_an_initial_segment — block.eraseDups.length = 64 ∧ ((List.range 36).all (fun n => block.contains n)) record
  4. repunit_divisibility_by_three_and_seven — ((List.range' 1 18).all (fun n => (repunit n % 3 == 0) == (n % 3 == 0))) ∧ ((List.range' 1 18).all (fun n => (repunit n % 7 == 0) == (n % 6 == 0))) record
  5. the_euler_characteristic_of_a_genus_g_surface — ((List.range 12).all (fun g => chi g + 2 * (g : Int) == 2)) ∧ chi 0 = 2 ∧ chi 1 = 0 ∧ chi 2 = -2 record
  6. odd_divisor_count_iff_perfect_square — (List.range' 1 120).all (fun n => ((divisors n).length % 2 == 1) == isSquare n) record
  7. havel_hakimi_decides_graphical_sequences — hh 12 [3, 3, 3, 3] = true ∧ hh 12 [2, 2, 2] = true ∧ hh 12 [3, 3, 1, 1] = false ∧ hh 12 [4, 1, 1, 1, 1] = true ∧ hh 12 [5, 1, 1, 1, 1] = false record
  8. the_euler_characteristic_of_a_genus_g_surface_for_every_g — ∀ g : Nat, chi g + 2 * (g : Int) = 2 record
  9. a_repunit_has_the_residue_of_its_length_mod_three — ∀ n : Nat, repunit n % 3 = n % 3 record
  10. a_repunit_is_divisible_by_three_exactly_when_its_length_is_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, (repunit n % 3 = 0) ↔ (n % 3 = 0) record
  11. repunit_of_a_sum — ∀ n k : Nat, repunit (n + k) = 10 ^ k * repunit n + repunit k record
  12. repunits_repeat_mod_seven_every_six_digits — ∀ n : Nat, repunit (n + 6) % 7 = repunit n % 7 record
  13. a_repunit_has_the_residue_of_its_length_mod_six_mod_seven — ∀ n : Nat, repunit n % 7 = repunit (n % 6) % 7 record
  14. a_repunit_is_divisible_by_seven_exactly_when_six_divides_its_length_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, (repunit n % 7 = 0) ↔ (n % 6 = 0) record
  15. the_two_coin_fare_is_minus_the_euler_characteristic_at_genus_two — (110 : Int) - 108 = - chi 2 record
  16. the_genus_reads_back_from_chi_for_every_g — ∀ g : Nat, ((2 - chi g) / 2).toNat = g record
  17. chi_is_injective_for_every_g_h — ∀ g h : Nat, chi g = chi h → g = h record
  18. a_repunit_is_below_ten_to_its_length — ∀ k : Nat, repunit k < 10 ^ k record
  19. a_repunit_splits_back_into_its_two_parts_for_every_n_k — ∀ n k : Nat, repunit (n + k) / 10 ^ k = repunit n ∧ repunit (n + k) % 10 ^ k = repunit k record
